classification.difficultyReason: Convert wall thickness, infer the inner radius and subtract inner from outer cylinder volumes.

inlines.text: Concrete sewer pipes are 5 m long with an outer diameter of 1.3 m.
The walls of the pipes are 10 cm thick. What volume of concrete is required to make each pipe?

spec.description: Hollow pipe receding from lower left to upper right, with near annular face, shaded bore, curved far silhouette, outer-diameter dimension, axial-length label and opposing wall-thickness leaders.
spec.mathematics: Outer radius 0.65 m; inner radius 0.55 m; length 5 m. The projected radial basis is perpendicular to the projected axis, with depth-compressed radial coordinate. Near and far end centres differ by the projected axis vector. Outer silhouette generators meet both end ellipses at their axis-parallel tangent points. The rear-facing opening is occluded. The inner-to-outer radius ratio is 11/13.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three source measurements are shown.

answer.worked:
Large cylinder − small cylinder.
$$\begin{align*}R&=\frac{1.3}{2}=0.65\text{ m}\\r&=0.65-0.10=0.55\text{ m}\\V&=\pi R^2h-\pi r^2h\\V&=\pi(0.65)^2(5)-\pi(0.55)^2(5)\\V&=0.6\pi\text{ m}^3\\V&\approx1.88\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$$
